::: {.cite-bar .domain-aid-sanctions}
[Repealed]{.status .status-repealed} [Pub. L. 116-92]{.cite} [133 Stat. 1198]{.cite} [22 U.S.C. 8791 note]{.cite}
:::

Imposed secondary sanctions on foreign persons doing business with the Assad government's military, energy, aviation, and reconstruction sectors. It was named for the military photographer who documented deaths in Syrian detention and was enacted as Title LXXIV of the FY2020 defense authorization.

## Key provisions

- Mandatory sanctions on foreign persons providing significant support to the Syrian government or to Russian and Iranian forces in Syria.
- Covered construction and engineering services for government-controlled reconstruction.
- Suspension and waiver conditions tied to an end to attacks on civilians, release of prisoners, and accountability.

## Why it matters

It shows the full life of a sanctions statute: enacted in a defense bill, extended, then repealed in a later one once the target government fell. Both steps ran through [the annual NDAA](ndaa-annual.qmd).

## Current status

Repealed by the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (Pub. L. 119-60), signed December 18, 2025, a year after the fall of the Assad government.
